records.source: וְלֹֽא־יָכֹ֨ל יוֹסֵ֜ף לְהִתְאַפֵּ֗ק לְכֹ֤ל הַנִּצָּבִים֙ עָלָ֔יו וַיִּקְרָ֕א הוֹצִ֥יאוּ כָל־אִ֖ישׁ מֵעָלָ֑י וְלֹא־עָ֤מַד אִישׁ֙ אִתּ֔וֹ בְּהִתְוַדַּ֥ע יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־אֶחָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And not was able Joseph to restrain himself before all those standing by him, and he called out, send out every man from with me. And not stood any man with him when made himself known Joseph to his brothers.
pieces: Joseph could hold back no longer in front of all the attendants around him. "Send everyone out of here!" he cried. So he was alone with his brothers when he told them who he was.

L.1: And Joseph could not restrain himself before all who stood by him, and he cried out, "Make everyone go out from me!" So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

R.1: Joseph could not keep his feelings in any longer in front of his servants. He shouted, "Everyone, leave the room!" So no one else was there when Joseph told his brothers who he was.

decisions.choice: restrain himself: hold in his feelings
decisions.reason: The same verb described Joseph controlling himself after weeping in 43:31. Now he can no longer hold back.

decisions.choice: made himself known: revealed his identity
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of yada, "know": Joseph lets himself be known. He does it in private, with no Egyptian witnesses to his brothers' shame.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ בִּבְכִ֑י וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע בֵּ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And he gave his voice in weeping, and heard Egypt, and heard [the] house of Pharaoh.
pieces: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard it, and word of it reached Pharaoh's household.

L.2: And he wept aloud, and the Egyptians heard, and the household of Pharaoh heard.

R.2: He cried so loudly that the Egyptians outside heard him. Even the people in Pharaoh's palace heard about it.

decisions.choice: gave his voice in weeping: wept aloud
decisions.reason: To "give one's voice" is to raise it; Joseph sobs out loud. This is the third and fullest time he weeps over his brothers (42:24; 43:30).

decisions.choice: Egypt heard: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: The name of the country stands for its people, here those in and around Joseph's house.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֤ף אֶל־אֶחָיו֙ אֲנִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף הַע֥וֹד אָבִ֖י חָ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָכְל֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ לַעֲנ֣וֹת אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֥י נִבְהֲל֖וּ מִפָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers, I [am] Joseph; [is] still my father living? And not were able his brothers to answer him, for they were terrified before him.
pieces: "I am Joseph!" he said to his brothers. "Is my father really still alive?" His brothers were too shaken to say a word, dismayed to be standing before him.

L.3: And Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified at his presence.

R.3: Joseph said to his brothers, "I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?" But his brothers could not say anything. They were too frightened of him.

decisions.choice: I am Joseph: the turning point
decisions.reason: Two Hebrew words undo twenty years of hiding. The brothers now stand before the brother they sold, who holds their lives in his hand.

decisions.choice: is my father still alive?: a question from the heart
decisions.reason: Joseph had already been told his father was alive (43:27-28). Now, speaking as a son, he asks again: "my father", not "your father".

decisions.choice: terrified: shaken, dismayed
decisions.reason: Bahal is sudden alarm or dismay. They fear what Joseph may do to them.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶל־אֶחָ֛יו גְּשׁוּ־נָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וַיִּגָּ֑שׁוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֲנִי֙ יוֹסֵ֣ף אֲחִיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: And said Joseph to his brothers, draw near, please, to me; and they drew near. And he said, I [am] Joseph your brother, whom you sold to Egypt.
pieces: Then Joseph said to his brothers, "Please, come closer." When they had come closer, he said, "I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.

L.4: And Joseph said to his brothers, "Please come near to me." And they came near. And he said, "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

R.4: Then Joseph said to them, "Please come close to me." When they did, he said, "I am your brother Joseph. I am the one you sold as a slave to be taken to Egypt.

decisions.choice: your brother, whom you sold: the truth named plainly
decisions.reason: Joseph does not hide what they did, but he calls himself their brother first.

decisions.choice: sold as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sale meant; "slave" stays, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph sold as a slave (37:27-28).

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀אַל־תֵּעָ֣צְב֗וּ וְאַל־יִ֨חַר֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־מְכַרְתֶּ֥ם אֹתִ֖י הֵ֑נָּה כִּ֣י לְמִֽחְיָ֔ה שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים לִפְנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And now, do not be grieved, and let it not burn in your eyes that you sold me here; for for preservation of life God sent me before you.
pieces: But now, do not be upset, and do not be angry with yourselves for selling me here. It was God who sent me on ahead of you, to keep people alive.

L.5: And now do not be distressed or angry with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you to preserve life.

R.5: But do not be upset or blame yourselves for selling me. God sent me here ahead of you to save people's lives.

decisions.choice: let it not burn in your eyes: do not be angry with yourselves
decisions.reason: Anger was pictured as burning. Here it is anger turned inward, self-reproach.

decisions.choice: God sent me to preserve life: God's purpose through human wrong
decisions.reason: Joseph does not deny the brothers sold him, but he sees God at work through their deed to keep many alive. He says it three times (verses 5, 7, 8) and again in 50:20. Psalm 105:17 says the same: God "sent a man before them".

decisions.choice: preservation of life: keeping people alive
decisions.reason: Michyah means the preserving of life, and so also the means to live, food (Judges 6:4). The famine context gives both senses.

records.source: כִּי־זֶ֛ה שְׁנָתַ֥יִם הָרָעָ֖ב בְּקֶ֣רֶב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְעוֹד֙ חָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין־חָרִ֖ישׁ וְקָצִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: For this two years [has been] the famine in [the] midst of the land, and still five years [in] which [there will be] no plowing and harvest.
pieces: The famine has now gripped the land for two years, and for five more years there will be no plowing and no harvest.

L.6: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.

R.6: There has been famine in the land for two years now. For five more years, no one will plow fields or gather crops.

decisions.choice: plowing and harvest: the whole farming year
decisions.reason: The two words cover the farming year from start to finish: with no rain or flood, nothing is sown and nothing reaped.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ לִפְנֵיכֶ֔ם לָשׂ֥וּם לָכֶ֛ם שְׁאֵרִ֖ית בָּאָ֑רֶץ וּלְהַחֲי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לִפְלֵיטָ֖ה גְּדֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And sent me God before you to make for you a remnant on the earth and to keep alive for you for a great deliverance.
pieces: God sent me ahead of you to make sure your family would survive on the earth, and to save your lives in a great act of rescue.

L.7: And God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to keep you alive by a great deliverance.

R.7: God sent me ahead of you to keep your family alive on the earth. He did it to save you in a wonderful way.

decisions.choice: remnant: those who survive
decisions.reason: She'erit is what remains after disaster, the survivors who carry on a family or people. The prophets later use the word for the faithful remnant of Israel (Isaiah 10:20-22).

decisions.choice: for a great deliverance: by a great rescue
alternatives: as a great company of survivors
decisions.reason: Peletah can mean an escape or rescue, or the band of those who escape. "To keep you alive by a great deliverance" is the more natural reading; "to keep alive for you many survivors" is possible.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹֽא־אַתֶּ֞ם שְׁלַחְתֶּ֤ם אֹתִי֙ הֵ֔נָּה כִּ֖י הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְשִׂימֵ֨נִֽי לְאָ֜ב לְפַרְעֹ֗ה וּלְאָדוֹן֙ לְכָל־בֵּית֔וֹ וּמֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And now, not you sent me here, but God; and he has made me a father to Pharaoh and lord of all his house and ruler over all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: So it was not really you who sent me here, but God. And he has made me a father to Pharaoh, master of his whole household and ruler of all Egypt.

L.8: So now it was not you who sent me here, but God. He has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

R.8: So it was not really you who sent me here. It was God. He has made me Pharaoh's most trusted adviser. I am in charge of his whole palace, and I rule over all of Egypt.

decisions.choice: father to Pharaoh: a title of a chief adviser
decisions.reason: "Father" was a title of honor for a trusted counselor (compare Judges 17:10; 2 Kings 6:21). It speaks of trust and authority, not age.

decisions.choice: Pharaoh's most trusted adviser
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title instead of keeping the picture.

records.source: מַהֲרוּ֮ וַעֲל֣וּ אֶל־אָבִי֒ וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֣ם אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ בִּנְךָ֣ יוֹסֵ֔ף שָׂמַ֧נִי אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאָד֖וֹן לְכָל־מִצְרָ֑יִם רְדָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹֽד׃
records.gloss: Hurry and go up to my father and you will say to him, thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.
pieces: Go up to my father quickly and tell him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me master of all Egypt. Come down to me without wasting any time.

L.9: Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, 'Thus says your son Joseph: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.

R.9: Now hurry back to my father. Tell him, 'Your son Joseph says: God has made me ruler of all Egypt. Come down to me right away.

decisions.choice: thus says: the formula of a messenger
decisions.reason: "Thus says" introduces a message delivered word for word for the sender, the form later used by the prophets ("thus says the LORD").

decisions.choice: God has made me lord: honor credited to God
decisions.reason: Joseph's message names God, not Pharaoh, as the one who raised him.

records.source: וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֣ בְאֶֽרֶץ־גֹּ֗שֶׁן וְהָיִ֤יתָ קָרוֹב֙ אֵלַ֔י אַתָּ֕ה וּבָנֶ֖יךָ וּבְנֵ֣י בָנֶ֑יךָ וְצֹאנְךָ֥ וּבְקָרְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And you will dwell in [the] land of Goshen and you will be near to me, you and your children and your children's children, and your flocks and your herds and all that [is] to you.
pieces: You can settle in the region of Goshen and be close to me, you and your children and grandchildren, your sheep and goats and cattle, and everything that belongs to you.

L.10: You shall live in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your children's children, your flocks and your herds and all that you have.

R.10: You can live in the land of Goshen, near me. Bring your children and grandchildren, your sheep, goats and cattle, and everything you own.

decisions.choice: Goshen: grazing land in the eastern Nile Delta
decisions.reason: Goshen lay in the northeast of Egypt, in the delta near the route to Canaan. It was good land for flocks and close to Joseph's seat of government.

decisions.choice: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Tson means a flock of small animals, sheep and goats together.

records.source: וְכִלְכַּלְתִּ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ שָׁ֔ם כִּי־ע֛וֹד חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים רָעָ֑ב פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֛שׁ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵֽיתְךָ֖ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And I will provide for you there, for still five years [of] famine, lest you become impoverished, you and your household and all that [is] to you.
pieces: I will supply your needs there, since there are still five years of famine ahead. Otherwise you, your family and all you have will end up in want.'

L.11: And I will provide for you there, for there are still five years of famine to come, so that you and your household and all that you have do not come to poverty.'

R.11: I will take care of you there. There will be five more years of famine, and I do not want you, your family and your animals to go hungry.'

decisions.choice: become impoverished: lose everything
decisions.reason: The verb means to be dispossessed or reduced to poverty.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֤ה עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ רֹא֔וֹת וְעֵינֵ֖י אָחִ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ין כִּי־פִ֖י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And here, your eyes [are] seeing and [the] eyes of my brother Benjamin, that my mouth [is] the [one] speaking to you.
pieces: You can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really I who am speaking to you.

L.12: And look, your eyes and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

R.12: You can see with your own eyes, and so can my brother Benjamin, that it is really me, Joseph, talking to you.

decisions.choice: my mouth speaks to you: no longer through an interpreter
decisions.reason: Until now Joseph had spoken to them through an interpreter (42:23). Now he speaks their own language directly, proof of who he is.

records.source: וְהִגַּדְתֶּ֣ם לְאָבִ֗י אֶת־כָּל־כְּבוֹדִי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר רְאִיתֶ֑ם וּמִֽהַרְתֶּ֛ם וְהוֹרַדְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־אָבִ֖י הֵֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: And you will tell my father all my honor in Egypt and all that you have seen; and you will hurry and bring down my father here.
pieces: Tell my father about all the honor I have in Egypt and everything you have seen. And hurry, bring my father down here."

L.13: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt and of all that you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here."

R.13: Tell my father how important I am in Egypt. Tell him everything you have seen. Then hurry and bring my father here."

decisions.choice: my honor: my high standing
decisions.reason: Kavod is weight, and so importance, honor and splendor. Here it is Joseph's rank and wealth in Egypt.

records.source: וַיִּפֹּ֛ל עַל־צַוְּארֵ֥י בִנְיָמִֽן־אָחִ֖יו וַיֵּ֑בְךְּ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן בָּכָ֖ה עַל־צַוָּארָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he fell on [the] neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
pieces: Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin and wept, and Benjamin wept as he embraced him.

L.14: And he fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

R.14: Then Joseph hugged his brother Benjamin and cried. Benjamin cried too as he hugged Joseph.

decisions.choice: fell on his neck: embraced him
decisions.reason: To fall on someone's neck is to throw one's arms around him (33:4; 46:29).

records.source: וַיְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְכָל־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּ֣בְךְּ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֣חֲרֵי כֵ֔ן דִּבְּר֥וּ אֶחָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them; and after that his brothers spoke with him.
pieces: He kissed each of his brothers and wept as he held them. Only then were his brothers able to talk with him.

L.15: And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them. After that his brothers talked with him.

R.15: Then he kissed all his brothers and cried as he hugged them. After that, his brothers began talking with him.

decisions.choice: his brothers spoke with him: a broken silence healed
decisions.reason: Years before, the brothers "could not speak peaceably to him" (37:4). Now they talk with him.

records.source: וְהַקֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמַ֗ע בֵּ֤ית פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֖אוּ אֲחֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And the report was heard [in the] house of Pharaoh, saying, have come [the] brothers of Joseph; and it was good in [the] eyes of Pharaoh and in [the] eyes of his servants.
pieces: News reached Pharaoh's palace that Joseph's brothers had arrived, and Pharaoh and his officials were glad.

L.16: And the report was heard in Pharaoh's house, "Joseph's brothers have come," and it pleased Pharaoh and his officials.

R.16: The news spread to Pharaoh's palace: "Joseph's brothers have come!" Pharaoh and his officials were happy to hear it.

decisions.choice: it was good in the eyes of: it pleased
decisions.reason: A common idiom for approval.

decisions.choice: officials
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's "servants" are his court, his high officials.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֱמֹ֥ר אֶל־אַחֶ֖יךָ זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ טַֽעֲנוּ֙ אֶת־בְּעִ֣ירְכֶ֔ם וּלְכוּ־בֹ֖אוּ אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And said Pharaoh to Joseph, say to your brothers, this do: load your animals and go, come to [the] land of Canaan,
pieces: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to load up their animals and return to the land of Canaan.

L.17: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Say to your brothers, 'Do this: load your animals and go back to the land of Canaan,

R.17: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and go back to Canaan.

decisions.choice: indirect speech
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn Pharaoh's message into reported instructions to avoid quotations within quotations; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: donkeys
decisions.reason: Be'ir means pack animals or livestock; the brothers' animals were donkeys (44:3, 13).

records.source: וּקְח֧וּ אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֛ם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּיכֶ֖ם וּבֹ֣אוּ אֵלָ֑י וְאֶתְּנָ֣ה לָכֶ֗ם אֶת־טוּב֙ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאִכְל֖וּ אֶת־חֵ֥לֶב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: and fetch your father and your households and come to me; and I will give to you [the] good of [the] land of Egypt, and you will eat [the] fat of the land.
pieces: They are to bring their father and their families and come to me. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they will live off the richest produce in the country.

L.18: and take your father and your households and come to me, and I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.'

R.18: Then they should bring their father and their families back here to me. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they will have plenty of good food to eat.

decisions.choice: the fat of the land: its richest produce
decisions.reason: Fat was the choicest part of an animal, so "the fat of the land" is the best that the land produces.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֥ה צֻוֵּ֖יתָה זֹ֣את עֲשׂ֑וּ קְחוּ־לָכֶם֩ מֵאֶ֨רֶץ מִצְרַ֜יִם עֲגָל֗וֹת לְטַפְּכֶם֙ וְלִנְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם וּנְשָׂאתֶ֥ם אֶת־אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וּבָאתֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, you are commanded: this do: take for yourselves from [the] land of Egypt carts for your little ones and for your wives, and you will carry your father and you will come.
pieces: And you are to give them this order as well: take carts from Egypt for their children and their wives, and bring their father here.

L.19: And you are commanded, 'Do this: take carts from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come.

R.19: Tell them also to take wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And they should bring their father here.

decisions.choice: you are commanded: Pharaoh authorizes Joseph
decisions.reason: Pharaoh tells Joseph that he, Joseph, is authorized to give this order to his brothers. The change from singular to plural in mid-sentence is abrupt, but the sense is clear.

decisions.choice: carts: wheeled wagons
decisions.reason: Agalot were two-wheeled carts pulled by oxen, common in Egypt but rare in the hill country of Canaan. Seeing them convinces Jacob (verse 27).

records.source: וְעֵ֣ינְכֶ֔ם אַל־תָּחֹ֖ס עַל־כְּלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּי־ט֛וּב כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָכֶ֥ם הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And your eye, let it not pity your belongings; for [the] good of all [the] land of Egypt, to you it [is].
pieces: They need not worry about the things they leave behind, because the best of all Egypt will be theirs."

L.20: Do not let your eye regret your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.'"

R.20: They should not worry about leaving things behind. The best of everything in Egypt will be theirs."

decisions.choice: let your eye not pity your things: do not mind leaving them
decisions.reason: The eye that "pities" looks back with regret. Pharaoh tells them not to be concerned for the goods they must leave in Canaan.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֥ם יוֹסֵ֛ף עֲגָל֖וֹת עַל־פִּ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָהֶ֛ם צֵדָ֖ה לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And did so [the] sons of Israel; and gave to them Joseph carts according to [the] mouth of Pharaoh, and he gave to them provisions for the way.
pieces: The sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them carts at Pharaoh's command, and supplies for the road.

L.21: And the sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them carts, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.

R.21: So Jacob's sons did this. Joseph gave them wagons, as Pharaoh had ordered, and food for the trip.

decisions.choice: according to the mouth of Pharaoh: at Pharaoh's command
decisions.reason: The "mouth" stands for what someone says or orders.

decisions.choice: the sons of Israel: Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: Israel is Jacob's God-given name (32:28). The phrase that becomes the name of the people still means Jacob's own sons here.

records.source: לְכֻלָּ֥ם נָתַ֛ן לָאִ֖ישׁ חֲלִפ֣וֹת שְׂמָלֹ֑ת וּלְבִנְיָמִ֤ן נָתַן֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת כֶּ֔סֶף וְחָמֵ֖שׁ חֲלִפֹ֥ת שְׂמָלֹֽת׃
records.gloss: To all of them he gave, to each man, changes of clothes; and to Benjamin he gave three hundred [of] silver and five changes of clothes.
pieces: He gave each of them a new set of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave {{units:about 7.5 pounds|300 shekels}} of silver and five sets of clothes.

L.22: To each and every one of them he gave changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave 300 [shekels] of silver and five changes of clothing.

R.22: He gave each of his brothers new clothes. But he gave Benjamin five sets of new clothes and {{units:about 7.5 pounds|300 shekels}} of silver.

decisions.choice: changes of clothes: fine garments for festive wear
decisions.reason: A "change" of clothing was a fine set to put on in place of everyday wear, a costly gift.

decisions.choice: more for Benjamin: favoritism without envy
decisions.reason: Joseph, once hated for his father's favor and his special robe (37:3-4), now openly favors Benjamin. The brothers' acceptance shows how far they have come.

decisions.choice: about 7.5 pounds of silver; with the Measures setting, 300 shekels
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "three hundred of silver"; shekels, about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams) each, are meant. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight by default; Literal keeps the original.

records.source: וּלְאָבִ֞יו שָׁלַ֤ח כְּזֹאת֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֲמֹרִ֔ים נֹשְׂאִ֖ים מִטּ֣וּב מִצְרָ֑יִם וְעֶ֣שֶׂר אֲתֹנֹ֡ת נֹֽ֠שְׂאֹת בָּ֣ר וָלֶ֧חֶם וּמָז֛וֹן לְאָבִ֖יו לַדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And to his father he sent according to this: ten donkeys carrying of [the] good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread and provision for his father for the way.
pieces: To his father he sent the same, and more: ten donkeys laden with the finest goods of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread and food for his father's journey.

L.23: And to his father he sent as follows: ten donkeys loaded with the good things of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread and provisions for his father for the journey.

R.23: He also sent his father ten donkeys carrying the best things from Egypt. And he sent ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread and other food for his father's trip.

decisions.choice: according to this: likewise, or as follows
decisions.reason: Kezot can mean "likewise" (gifts like those just given) or "as follows" (introducing the list). Either way the list follows.

records.source: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַֽל־תִּרְגְּז֖וּ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And he sent off his brothers and they went, and he said to them, do not be agitated on the way.
pieces: Then he sent his brothers off, and as they left he told them, "Do not argue with each other on the way."

L.24: So he sent his brothers away, and they departed, and he said to them, "Do not quarrel on the way."

R.24: Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way. As they left he said, "Do not fight with each other on the trip!"

decisions.choice: do not quarrel: or, do not be afraid
decisions.reason: Ragaz means to be stirred up or agitated, whether by anger or by fear. Joseph may be warning them not to blame one another over the past, or reassuring them that they have nothing to fear on the road. The first fits the brothers' history (42:22).

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they went up from Egypt and came [to the] land of Canaan to Jacob their father.
pieces: So they left Egypt and went up to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan.

L.25: And they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.

R.25: They left Egypt and went back to their father Jacob in Canaan.

records.source: וַיַּגִּ֨דוּ ל֜וֹ לֵאמֹ֗ר ע֚וֹד יוֹסֵ֣ף חַ֔י וְכִֽי־ה֥וּא מֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיָּ֣פָג לִבּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י לֹא־הֶאֱמִ֖ין לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they told him, saying, still Joseph [is] alive, and that he [is] ruling over all [the] land of Egypt. And grew numb his heart, for not did he believe them.
pieces: "Joseph is alive!" they told him. "He is governor of the whole land of Egypt!" Jacob was stunned; he could not believe them.

L.26: And they told him, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt." And his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.

R.26: They told him, "Joseph is still alive! He is the ruler of all Egypt!" Jacob was so shocked that he felt nothing. He did not believe them.

decisions.choice: his heart grew numb: he was stunned
decisions.reason: Puq means to grow cold or numb. The news is too great for Jacob to take in.

records.source: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֵ֣ת כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֤י יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־הָ֣עֲגָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־שָׁלַ֥ח יוֹסֵ֖ף לָשֵׂ֣את אֹת֑וֹ וַתְּחִ֕י ר֖וּחַ יַעֲקֹ֥ב אֲבִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they spoke to him all [the] words of Joseph which he had spoken to them; and he saw the carts which Joseph had sent to carry him, and revived [the] spirit of Jacob their father.
pieces: But when they repeated to him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the carts Joseph had sent to carry him, their father Jacob's spirit came back to life.

L.27: But when they told him all the words that Joseph had spoken to them, and when he saw the carts that Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.

R.27: But then they told him everything Joseph had said to them. And Jacob saw the wagons Joseph had sent to bring him to Egypt. Then their father Jacob felt alive again.

decisions.choice: his spirit revived: life and hope returned
decisions.reason: Ruach, "spirit" or "breath", is a person's vital energy. Jacob, who had expected to go down to Sheol mourning (37:35), comes back to life.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל רַ֛ב עוֹד־יוֹסֵ֥ף בְּנִ֖י חָ֑י אֵֽלְכָ֥ה וְאֶרְאֶ֖נּוּ בְּטֶ֥רֶם אָמֽוּת׃
records.gloss: And said Israel, enough! Still Joseph my son [is] alive. I will go and see him before I die.
pieces: "Enough!" said Israel. "My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die."

L.28: And Israel said, "It is enough; Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."

R.28: Then Israel said, "Now I believe it! My son Joseph is still alive! I will go and see him before I die."

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob's covenant name
decisions.reason: The narrator switches from "Jacob" (verse 27) to "Israel" as the father revives and decides to go. The name God gave him (32:28; 35:10) marks him as the father of the people.

decisions.choice: enough: I am convinced, I need nothing more
decisions.reason: Rav here expresses that Jacob needs no further proof; or perhaps that this one fact is all he asks.
